Angered by the [Kansas–Nebraska Act](/wiki/Kansas%E2%80%93Nebraska_Act "Kansas–Nebraska Act") of 1854, which opened the territories to slavery, he became a leader of the new [Republican Party](/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"). Common dice are small [cubes](/wiki/Cube "Cube"), most often 1.6 cm (0.63 in) across, whose faces are numbered from one to six, usually by patterns of round dots called [pips](/wiki/Pip_(counting) "Pip (counting)"). (While the use of [Arabic numerals](/wiki/Arabic_numerals "Arabic numerals") is occasionally seen, such dice are less common.)

Opposite sides of a modern die traditionally add up to seven, requiring the one ([![1](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Die_face_1b.svg/40px-Die_face_1b.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Die_face_1b.svg)), two ([![2](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Die_face_2b.svg/40px-Die_face_2b.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Die_face_2b.svg)), and three ([![3](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Die_face_3b.svg/40px-Die_face_3b.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Die_face_3b.svg)) faces to share a [vertex](/wiki/Vertex_(geometry) "Vertex (geometry)").[[22]](#cite_note-22) The faces of a die may be placed [clockwise or counterclockwise](/wiki/Clockwise "Clockwise") about this vertex. If the one ([![1](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Die_face_1b.svg/40px-Die_face_1b.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Die_face_1b.svg)), two ([![2](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Die_face_2b.svg/40px-Die_face_2b.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Die_face_2b.svg)), and three ([![3](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Die_face_3b.svg/40px-Die_face_3b.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Die_face_3b.svg)) faces run counterclockwise, the die is called "right-handed". If those faces run clockwise, the die is called "left-handed". Western dice are normally right-handed, and Chinese dice are normally left-handed.[[23]](#cite_note-diceplay-23)
